entities.summary: Bertold of Regensburg, also known as Berthold of Ratisbon, was a German preacher and canon lawyer who played a significant role in the development of medieval canon law and the Reformation. Born in the early 13th century, Bertold was a prominent figure in the Catholic Church, serving as a canon at the Cathedral of Regensburg and later as a member of the Council of Ratisbon. He was a key figure in the drafting of the Decretum Gratiani, a foundational text of canon law that shaped the Church's legal framework for centuries. Bertold's influence extended beyond the Church, as he was also a prominent advocate for the rights of the Church and its clergy. His work had a lasting impact on the development of Western law and the Reformation, which continues to shape the course of modern history. The legacy of Bertold of Regensburg serves as a testament to the enduring power of his ideas and the significance of his contributions to the development of medieval canon law and the Reformation.
